items.title: Artifacts — implementation plan and tracking
items.description: ## Goal This issue is the implementation plan and tracker for **artifacts**: versioned deliverables an agent publishes from its workspace. People open them in the console, ask the agent to revise them, and share one revision at a time. Artifacts are owned by people, not by agents or sessions, and outlive both. Design: [docs/designs/artifacts.md](https://github.com/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/blob/main/docs/designs/artifacts.md) (#4441). Terms (Artifact, Revision, Artifact share) are in [GLOSSARY.md](https://github.com/agentconnect-md/agentconnect/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md). ## Test environment URL: `https://test-app.agentconnect.md` (console, org `agentconnect`) · API: `https://test-api.agentconnect.md/v1` Deploy signal: every non-docs merge to `main` runs the **Release** workflow (`release.yaml`), which cuts a `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` tag; the test cluster's control plane, web and daemon pool roll to it within minutes (check the deployment images in namespace `agentconnect-test` against `git tag --contains `). Test account: the console session kept in the verification browser profile; no credentials are recorded here. Daemon-side changes are verified with an agent on the Cloud daemon pool, which follows the rc. ## Phase 1 — Publish and open (L) After this phase an agent can publish and a person can open the result. It covers single-file HTML, Markdown, images, PDF and source, and every byte path keeps "nothing renders on the bucket's origin". Acceptance (verified in test env): - [x] In a webchat session with a Cloud agent, asking the agent to publish an HTML file leaves an artifact card in the transcript, and the reply carries a console link to it. - [x] Opening the card or the link shows the page running in a sandboxed frame; a Markdown file renders as a document, an image and a PDF display, source is highlighted, and a DOCX offers download only. - [x] Asking for a change produces revision 2 with its own card; the revision-1 card says a newer revision exists, and the viewer's revision menu switches between them. - [x] Download returns a single file as itself, and a multi-file revision (a PDF entry with its DOCX original) as a zip. - [x] The agent fetches an earlier revision back into `outputs/` and publishes a revision built from it. - [x] The link opened by a member outside a private session's audience shows "no access". items.title: Add a toxval_predict() method for glm fits, tested on the CO2 seep data
items.description: ## What Add a `toxval_predict()` method for models fitted with `stats::glm()`, so `ecx()` and `nsec()` accept a glm directly. Test it against one NSEC from Noonan et al. (2025), reproduced from the public AIMS data. The vignette built on that case study is part of #71. This is the first part of #21; `gam`, `glmer` and the other classes it lists are out of scope here. ## Why it matters Noonan et al. (2025, *Communications Biology* 8:1518, ) report 29 NSECs from glm fits of reef benthos against aragonite saturation state (ΩAr). Because toxval had no glm method, they were computed with custom code calling the internal `toxval:::nsec_fct()`. That code takes the reference from a pointwise Wald band and returns no interval on the NSEC. #43 sets out why inverting a pointwise band does not give an interval on the predictor. Under the refactor (`REFACTOR-human.md` §3.3–3.4), a glm needs one method and nothing else, since `boot_parms()` already draws from `MVN(coef, vcov)`. A prototype of that method, run on the published data, gives the published NSEC and adds an interval. The case study is a field gradient, not a laboratory exposure. The ambient condition is at the high end of the predictor and the stressor increases as ΩAr falls. This tests whether the package handles a reference that is not the lowest predictor value, which the existing `drc` and `brms` examples do not. ## Proposed decisions 1. The method accepts a glm whose formula contains the predictor and, optionally, one grouping factor named by `group_var`. A fit with an offset or with further covariates is refused in this issue, because the grid gives no value for them. Any class inheriting from `glm` that is not a plain glm is refused unless listed as supported, because `mgcv::gam` fits have class `c("gam", "glm", "lm")` and would otherwise dispatch here and return wrong curves. `MASS::glm.nb` (`c("negbin", "glm", "lm")`) is accepted, with theta treated as fixed, and this is documented. 2. The case study fits on the reduction from ambient, `om_deficit = 3.5 - OmAr.mean`, with `x_range = c(0, max(om_deficit))`, so that the control is the first grid value, as every compute function requires. No argument for a reference inside the data range is added here. The inconsistency described under Evidence is recorded for #21 to settle. 3. A glm with family `binomial` or `quasibinomial` is a proportion bounded at 1, so the increasing `absolute` reference is taken towards 1 (T18). This needs a glm branch in `respons

items.title: Adopt a three-layer rule model and review DistSSHRun-derived defaults before 0.1
items.description: ## Proposal (decision pending) Adopt the three-layer rule model from [#58](https://github.com/yamanori99/AgentRuleLint.jl/issues/58) (core, opt-in presets, and `project_rules`), including promotion criteria, a visible exact vs heuristic classification, and a pre-0.1 review of DistSSHRun-derived defaults. ### Layers and promotion - **Core** (on by default, pinned by edition): only exact rules, or rules with almost no false positives, intended for the community at large. - **Presets** (opt-in, versioned per preset): bundles of a particular discipline, including our own projects. - **`project_rules`**: promises that only make sense in one repository, managed by that project. A new rule starts as a `project_rule` or a preset in our own project, and is promoted to core only after: 1. A period of use in our own project with no reported false positives. 2. Golden and adversarial corpora exist. 3. It does not overlap existing tools (JETLS, Aqua, and similar). See [#49](https://github.com/yamanori99/AgentRuleLint.jl/issues/49). 4. Its classification as exact or heuristic is settled. Community false-positive reports are added to the corpus following CONTRIBUTING.md and serve as both promotion evidence and regression tests. Existing proposals [#34](https://github.com/yamanori99/AgentRuleLint.jl/issues/34)–[#44](https://github.com/yamanori99/AgentRuleLint.jl/issues/44) should be classified under this model. No per-proposal decision is made here. Visibility of `project_rules` versus built-in rules remains [#48](https://github.com/yamanori99/AgentRuleLint.jl/issues/48). ### Exact vs heuristic, shown in docs and `explain` - **Exact:** diffs, file paths, and config values (`protected-paths`, the ceiling ratchet, `scope-paths`, deletion of test files or testsets). False positives should not arise in principle. - **Heuristic:** rules that step into the meaning of the code (string-splitting evasions, trivially true tests). Completeness is not a goal (Rice's theorem); the aim is to raise the cost of naive evasions and to make them visible in review. That classification should appear in the docs and in `explain` output. The requirement “do not let the check itself be disabled” is guaranteed on the exact-rule side. ### Pre-0.1 review of DistSSHRun-derived defaults Before publishing 0.1, review the defaults from a first-time Julia package's point of view and drop assumptions that do not belong in the default. ### Evidence (origin/main `028df3a`) - Auto-protected paths in `src/ru

items.title: Read ecx() and nsec() per observed level of a grouping that spans the series
items.description: ## What This is the `toxval` half of open-AIMS/bayesnec#554, which applies one rule to both packages. A grouping spans the concentration series when each of its levels is observed across the series, as plates, batches, repeated runs or genotypes usually are. A grouping is nested within concentration when each level is observed at a single concentration, as replicate cells, tanks or chambers are. For a fit with a group-level term on a grouping that spans the series, such as `(1 | plate)` in a `brm()` formula or `ogl(plate)` in a `bnec()` fit, `toxval_predict()` will predict the curve of each observed level, including that level's deviations, with any nested term at zero. `ecx()` and `nsec()` then read each level against its own control and pool the levels through the `pool` argument of #96, with `"mixture"` as the default for such a grouping. At present every method predicts with `re_formula = NA`, and a `group_var` that appears only in a group-level term is refused. `x_control` also gains two values, `"own"` and `"shared"`, which set whether each group or level reads its control at its own lowest concentration or at one concentration shared by all of them. Its numeric value keeps its present meaning, and `bayesnec` gains the same value, so that `x_control = 0` reads the control at zero concentration in both packages. ## Why it matters The NSEC reference is the `sig_val` quantile of the control realisations. On the curve with every group-level deviation at zero, those realisations include the uncertainty in the mean of a deviation that every concentration of a level shares, such as the gain of a plate reader. That uncertainty says nothing about whether a response differs from its control. On the `lum31` zinc data of the `bayesnec` vignette `example8`, with 17 plates under `ogl(plate)`, the NSEC read this way corresponds to a 24 per cent effect, against 3.4 per cent when it is read from each observed plate (open-AIMS/bayesnec#554 gives the measurements). Fisher and Fox (2023) define the NSEC by a comparison with the control within one experiment, where a shared deviation cancels. The two packages must also give the same value for the same fitted object. open-AIMS/bayesnec#554 changes `bayesnec`'s estimators. Without this issue, `toxval::nsec()` and `bayesnec::nsec()` would disagree on every `bnec()` fit with such a term, and `toxval`'s `brmsfit` method would follow a different rule from its `bayesnec` methods. items.title: feat: cap tool output (2,000 lines / 50 KB) and spill the full output to a file
items.description: ## Problem Tool output is appended to the conversation in full. `read` loads the whole file (`marvin/tools/coding.py:23-72`), `exec` buffers all stdout and stderr (`coding.py:264-267`), `web_fetch` and `browser_fetch` have no size cap. One test log or large file can exceed the context window, and the resulting API error is then reported as success (see the failed-runs issue). The only cap in the codebase is 10,000 characters in the `browser` tool. Both reference harnesses use the same numbers: - pi `coding-agent/src/core/tools/truncate.ts:11-12`: 2,000 lines or 50 KB. File reads keep the head with a hint (`[Showing lines A-B of N. Use offset=X to continue.]`, `tools/read.ts:331-340`); command output keeps the tail and the full output is written to a temp file named in the notice. - opencode `core/src/tool-output.ts:13-14`: the same caps applied by the runner after every tool; full output saved and the preview ends with `[showing lines 1-N of M; full output saved to ]`. `read` also caps each line at 2,000 characters. Reference commits: pi `badlogic/pi-mono@a40abec`, opencode `sst/opencode@1017760` (both 2026-11-11). Paths below are relative to each repo's `packages/`. marvin paths are on `main` (`b0bc11c`). ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] A single cap (default 2,000 lines / 50 KB, configurable) is applied to every tool result before it enters the conversation - [ ] `read` keeps the head and tells the model which `offset` continues the file; very long single lines are cut - [ ] `exec` and `process` keep the tail; the full output is written to a file in a per-run directory and the notice gives its path - [ ] `web_fetch` and `browser_fetch` are capped the same way - [ ] The truncation notice states how much was shown and how much exists - [ ] `read` streams or bounds its file access instead of loading an arbitrarily large file into memory - [ ] Tests cover head and tail truncation, the spill file, and an untruncated small result ### Added by readiness review - [ ] The cap applies to the model-visible text (`ToolResult.to_model_content()`), including the error suffix, so error output is capped too. The final marker is never cut off by the cap itself - [ ] "50 KB" is measured in bytes of UTF-8; truncation never splits a multibyte character - [ ] The cap is configurable through one setting each for max lines and max bytes (env var names to be fixed in the plan, documented in the README and the `CLAUDE.md` env table) - [ ] The per-run spill directory is created lazil

items.title: Nulavio is promoted with a trailer, feature shorts and launch material: AI voice, music and motion over real recordings, honest and disclosed
items.description: ## Problem Nulavio has a public alpha, a waitlist and a site, but nothing that spreads the word: no trailer, no short clips, no launch posts, no material for the press or for app stores. The maintainer wants promotion at the highest quality possible, using AI where it helps: generated voice-over, music, sound effects and motion graphics, and scripted mouse movement over real recordings. ## Rules: what makes this trustworthy The brand's promise is "honest by design" ([strategy](../blob/main/docs/brand/strategy.md)). Marketing that breaks it would cost more than it brings. 1. **The product is always real.** Anything that shows Nulavio's interface or behaviour is recorded from a real build, by a script. AI may make the voice, the music, sound effects, titles, transitions and abstract backgrounds. It never makes images of the interface or of results the browser does not produce. 2. **Claims have evidence.** Every claim in a script, post or caption links to the test, ADR or document that backs it, in the spirit of the site's `test_copy_is_honest`. Planned features are marked as planned. There are no absolute claims ("100% private") and no comparisons without a dated source. 3. **No fake people.** No invented testimonials, reviews, user counts or press quotes. No accounts posing as users and no AI-written comments posted as if from the community. No synthetic voice imitating a real person; a recognisable human voice only with that person's written consent. 4. **AI is disclosed.** Each video says that its voice and music are AI-generated, and platforms' AI-content labels are set where they exist (for example YouTube's "altered or synthetic content"). 5. **Licences are recorded.** Each generated asset's tool, plan, date and terms of commercial use are kept next to the asset in a manifest, like the site's screenshot manifest. Tools whose terms do not allow commercial use, or keep rights over the output, are not used. Open models (TTS such as Piper or Kokoro, motion tools such as Motion Canvas) are preferred where their quality is enough. 6. **Neutral about third parties.** No third-party service (search engine, password manager, AI provider) is shown as part of Nulavio or as the recommended choice, and no partnership is implied. Mozilla and Firefox are named only as the [strategy](../blob/main/docs/brand/strategy.md#correct-use-of-the-name-and-marks) allows, with the "not affiliated" line. 7. **Privacy in recordings.** Only test profiles, fixture sites and test acc

items.title: nulavio.net is redesigned with motion and real recordings of the browser, still static and first-party
items.description: ## Problem nulavio.net works and is honest, but it is static: text, still screenshots and tables. It does not show the browser moving: a profile opening, a protected profile unlocking, a link routed to the right profile, a search provider chosen in one step, a highlight link opening on the passage. Pages for other browsers do show this. The maintainer wants a site that looks more professional, has motion and recordings, and helps promote Nulavio. This starts **after the Orion features plan (#172) is finished**. Its features are part of what the new site has to show. ## Constraints that stay These come from the current site and its tests (`tests/unit/test_site.py`, `site/_headers`). The redesign keeps them, or the maintainer changes them on purpose: - **No scripts and no third parties.** The CSP has no `script-src`, and the test refuses ` `. Motion is done with CSS: transitions, `@keyframes`, and scroll-driven animations as progressive enhancement, so a page is complete without them. Allowing a first-party script needs a maintainer decision, recorded with its reason. - **Video needs a CSP change.** `default-src 'none'` blocks ` ` today. The redesign adds `media-src 'self'` only, with files hosted on the same origin. There are no YouTube or Vimeo embeds. - **Honest copy** (`test_copy_is_honest`): no invented testimonials, user counts or audits. Forward-looking claims follow the existing "No fine print" rule. - **Real captures.** Screenshots come from the real build through `scripts/site/capture_site.py`, with hashes in the manifest and transcripts on the page. Recordings follow the same rule: they are recorded from a Nulavio build by a script, reproducibly, with captions and a transcript. - **Both languages**, with the same ids in pt-BR and en. The waitlist, the download pages and the deploy through `.github/workflows/site.yml` keep working. ## Plan 1. **References.** A dated moodboard of 8–10 sites, browser sites (Arc, Zen, Vivaldi, Orion, Mullvad Browser, Brave) and product sites known for motion (Linear, Raycast, Things and the like). For each, note what to borrow (structure, rhythm, how motion explains the product) and what to avoid (weight, scripts, trackers). Kept in `docs/design/`. 2. **Directions.** Two or three visual directions inside the brand (`docs/brand/guidelines.md`, `tokens.json`), each with a mock-up of the home page in light and dark and a motion sketch. **The maintainer chooses one.** 3. **Recordings.** A script records short scenes from

items.title: The brand is reviewed: no lockup reads "N nulavio", and colours, symbol and app icon are checked where people see them
items.description: ## Problem The horizontal lockup (`docs/brand/assets/logo/nulavio-lockup-horizontal*.svg`), used at the top of the README and in the site header, puts the symbol, an **N**, next to the wordmark **nulavio**. Together they read as "N nulavio", so the initial appears twice. Some brands pair a letter symbol with the full name on purpose. Here, though, the maintainer noticed it as a fault, so the lockup is not working as intended. The maintainer also wants to review the brand as a whole: colours, symbol, app icon and lockups. Today's brand, "A — Obsidian Current" with the "Vanishing Route" symbol and a Mint/Navy palette, was chosen on 2026-10-24 against weighted criteria ([explorations](../blob/main/docs/brand/explorations.md), [guidelines](../blob/main/docs/brand/guidelines.md)). That was before the site, the README and the store listings existed, and it was checked mostly at small sizes and in contrast pairs. ## Scope: the maintainer decides | Option | What changes | Cost | |---|---|---| | **a. Lockup only** | The horizontal lockup stops repeating the N: the wordmark alone where the name is shown, the symbol alone as the icon; or the symbol drawn as the wordmark's first letter | Small: the logo scripts and their consumers | | **b. Refresh** | (a), plus the palette and the symbol revised and the app icon redrawn, keeping the name and the brand's ideas (route, null, the trail that fades) | Medium: tokens and every surface that uses them | | **c. Rebrand** | A new visual identity. The name stays: the domain, the GitHub organization, the app ID `net.nulavio.Nulavio` and the trademark searches are all built on it | Large | Recommendation: start with (b). Do (a) right away if the review takes long, so the README and the site stop showing "N nulavio". ## Plan 1. **Audit with evidence.** Today's brand shown where people meet it: the README in light and dark, the site header, the KDE panel and launcher at 16–48 px, the app's about dialog, the GNOME Software and Flathub listing, the F-Droid listing and the Android launcher (Companion), link previews (OG image), and the social profiles: the X account [x.com/getnulavio](https://x.com/getnulavio), created by the maintainer on 2026-11-16, with its avatar in the circle crop and its header banner. Each problem gets a screenshot. 2. **References.** A dated moodboard of browser and privacy brands (Orion, Arc, Zen, Mullvad, Proton, Brave, Vivaldi, Tor), noting what makes each one recognisable and what Nulavio should avoid: padl

items.title: Keeper: Fiber delegates run under the keeper, and the process-tree walk counts it
items.description: > *This was generated by AI during triage.* Part 2 of #3890, split on 2026-11-02 (ruling 6591558689). It is blocked by #3890 (Part 1, the shell path) and by the owner's ruling on the process-tree walk. ## What to build - Fiber delegates start under the session's keeper, as `docs/tools.md` "The keeper" and `docs/delegates.md` "Lifetime" state. While the parent is gone, a Fiber delegate that ends gets its `job_completed` from the keeper, and the resumed parent writes `delegate_finished` from the delegate's own log. - A resumed session reuses the handed-over keeper for new commands. Remove the known-limit line Part 1 adds to `docs/tools.md` "One keeper per session". - The process-tree walk, as the owner rules on #3890 (options in comment 6591254754: A, the keeper counts on the walk; B, Fiber delegates stay session children; C, redesign). With A, this part adds the parent exemption for delegates under a keeper and edits `docs/permissions.md` "Sessions on the sockets". Part 1 has already added `fiber keeper` to the session processes and the keeper pid to the session's own set. - Plan Task 6 (the hosted delegate), the `delegates.rs` test rewrites, `Registry::host` and the `delegate_end` re-export in `crates/jobs/src/lib.rs`, from `fiber-3890-plan-1.md` in flywheel's run directory. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Binary-level test: start a session that runs one Fiber delegate, SIGKILL the session process while the delegate runs, let it finish, then resume. The resumed session's log and next turn carry the delegate's result (`delegate_finished`), and there is no `orphaned`. - [ ] Binary-level test: a session's `delegate_message` reaches a Fiber delegate that is under its keeper, and a shell command the session started is still refused `from_session` when it steers that delegate. - [ ] Binary-level test: after a handover, a new command runs under the old keeper, and its hub `reply` is refused `from_session`. - [ ] `scripts/check` passes. Needs a planner. It changes a permissions rule, so its PR needs the owner's ruling on #3890 first. Blocked by #3890 Written against 0a94c21f9

items.title: Add agent-chatter phrases for your language (noise-lang)
items.description: Memoria drops agent chatter ("let me check…", "want me to…", "hope this helps") before it becomes a memory. Those phrases are per language, in plain JSON files. No regex or engine code is needed. Today there are two: English (`en.json`) and Indonesian (`id.json`). If you write to your AI tools in another language, its chatter currently slips through as junk memories. **What to do** 1. Copy `src/engine/extract/noise-lang/en.json` to ` .json` (ISO 639-1, e.g. `es.json`, `hi.json`, `pt.json`, `de.json`, `ja.json`). 2. Set `language` and `name`, keep each rule `id` and `at` as they are, and write the phrases an AI agent typically says in your language. Natural phrasing beats a literal translation. 3. Add one import line in `src/engine/extract/noise-lang/index.ts` and add the file to `LANGUAGE_FILES`. 4. Optional but very welcome: add a few real examples to `tests/fixtures/heuristic-eval.json`. **Check** `tests/noise-lang.test.mjs` validates every language file. One language per PR. Comment below with the language you are taking so two people don't do the same one.

items.title: Linux on ARM64 as a build host: an ILCompiler of the host's architecture and a linux-arm64 tools bundle
items.description: A Linux machine with an ARM64 processor cannot build a Cosmos kernel today: a Raspberry Pi 5, Asahi Linux, an ARM64 VM, or this repository's devcontainer on an Apple Silicon Mac (its base image has a `linux/arm64` variant). #3420 made Windows on ARM a supported host, which leaves Linux on ARM64 as the one host family without tools. It takes more than a bundle. The SDK starts an x64 ILCompiler on every host, and where macOS has Rosetta 2 and Windows 11 its x64 emulation, Linux has nothing of its own to run it with. Nobody has asked for this yet. Nothing below was run on a Linux ARM64 machine: it is read from the targets, the workflow and the CI logs of the other hosts. ## What happens today - **The ILCompiler is x64 whatever the host.** `Cosmos.Build.Ilc.targets` resolves `runtime. -x64.Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler` ([L24](https://github.com/CosmosOS/Cosmos/blob/5a5356e1102a36c7f7b568422c8bdf2ba25d9dde/src/Cosmos.Build.Ilc/build/Cosmos.Build.Ilc.targets#L24)). `Sdk.props` downloads the same package through `HostRuntimeIdentifier`, which is `win-x64`, `linux-x64` or `osx-x64` ([L108-L121](https://github.com/CosmosOS/Cosmos/blob/5a5356e1102a36c7f7b568422c8bdf2ba25d9dde/src/Cosmos.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.props#L108-L121)). `Sdk.targets` has a second resolution target, `ResolveIlcPath`, with a list of its own ([L116-L140](https://github.com/CosmosOS/Cosmos/blob/5a5356e1102a36c7f7b568422c8bdf2ba25d9dde/src/Cosmos.Sdk/Sdk/Sdk.targets#L116-L140)). None of the three reads the host architecture. The `windows-11-arm` leg of .NET Tests shows it: its [log](https://github.com/CosmosOS/Cosmos/actions/runs/44411769500/job/135200531734) reads `HostILCompilerPack: runtime.win-x64.Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler`. On Linux ARM64 that `ilc` is an x86-64 binary the system cannot start. - **`cosmos install` takes the x64 archives.** `GetPlatformTarget` answers `linux-x64` for every Linux ([L279-L287](https://github.com/CosmosOS/Cosmos/blob/5a5356e1102a36c7f7b568422c8bdf2ba25d9dde/src/Cosmos.Tools/Commands/InstallCommand.cs#L279-L287)), and `InstallTargetTests` pins that answer ([L14](https://github.com/CosmosOS/Cosmos/blob/5a5356e1102a36c7f7b568422c8bdf2ba25d9dde/tests/Cosmos.Tests.Tools/InstallTargetTests.cs#L14)). - **`tools-latest` has no `linux-arm64` archive.** ## What is missing 1. **An ILCompiler of the host's architecture.** The package exists: `runtime.linux-arm64.Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler` is published for the same 16 stable versions as the x64 one, 10.0.0 to 10.0.15. .NET documents

items.title: Ask HN: Coworker rejects PR (a month in) because it does not meet his standards
items.description: just joined this new team about 1 year into their development. Demoed the work to the team about two weeks ago (half way in). Work is practically complete & runs well no issues. I create PR & assign the two PR reviewers (one my rank another a rank above me). one colleague (the one at my level) leaves some constructive comments no functional changes. The other colleague (one rank above me) says something equivalent to "does not meet our standards" "do not do x pattern since we have used y (which has a huge limitation)" to use Y pattern I would basically need to change most of the logic and it would be about 70% waste. I demoed my code with this pattern two weeks ago and there were no issues/comments from the team. The code is concise and easy to read. I had a call with the colleague and explained the code and why I used it, and showed him some other parts of the codebase where this pattern should be used, his only defense was that "it does not meet our standards because it uses X rather than y pattern, since we used y pattern in the past, we should only use y pattern" while x pattern is very similar only removing the limitation that was causing the code to be difficult to maintain etc. This "standard requirement" is written nowhere as a hard requirement and the codebase is barely one year old, with only one of the codebase founders still on the team.... I'm going to have a chat with the manager tomorrow morning.

items.title: Ask HN: Am I the only one whose AI hype is cooling down a lot?
items.description: I am in the industry for 15+ years, studied CS, and actually, never really "liked" programming. It was a means to an end. I have written about programming (and published books), so don't get me wrong: I like the craft and I miss the sense of accomplishment after hours and days of struggling and fixing a problem with 2 lines of code. What I see in my personal spending and habits: I get free tokens from my company, and I spent between 3k-5k a month at the start of the year. Models got cheaper, but also: The usefullness ran its course a little bit for me. I still don't write code by hand, but when doing research, finding solutions, even some decisions (using Opus 5.5 and Astra 6.2 for example) are more and more questionable. I handed large research tasks to models, but even small questions like: "What do you think about these PR comments pointing out issues" (I need to be vague, working for a larger company), it didn't find even basic facts I found via Google and reading the docs for 2mins. I usually did higher level thinking, researched with the model, and then went to the implementation phase. But lately, I am not happy with both the research results (I continuesly have to narrow it down, go back, refine... I spend a day or 2 days refining, which in the end, I can do by myself now and actually feel a sense of accomplishment). Even the implementation isn't all that great. Maybe my bar for acceptable work is higher now, since these tools are not "magic" anymore. I think I gave them more leeway in the beginning because they wowed me. But now... not so much anymore. I even dread opening up Claude Code or Codex and I'd rather read and write code myself, and just give them smaller tasks, or once I nailed it down, I let a large chunk of code write by a model (because it "types" faster...). Am I alone? I read a lot of think pieces, I have agents working on my private dedicated server to maintain my machine and set up my self-hosting services. But more and more, I'd rather.... do it myself again, be more precise, and use it as a workhorse instead of a thinking researcher.

items.title: Ask HN: For professional Mathematicians –- about your career in the future
items.description: Hi friends, genuine question. We all see that top notch Mathematicians can use LLM to prove world class results in a relatively short time of period. OK I admit some of the results are not verified yet, but please hear me. Neither do I know how much “brain” is human and how much is the LLM, because we don’t see the prompts. My question is: what do you think about your career in the future? Please hear me out. In the current world, the way you become a Mathematician, is to get good scores, go to schools, take PHD and then professorship. There may be middle steps like postdoctoral or industry experience, but that’s the general way to do it. And the way that schools judge professors, if I understand correctly, is more about how much results you can get —- ofc if you can obtain big grants then the better, but most of you can’t do that, so I assume that it’s more about the papers. You also teach but that’s not as big as the research. For now, there are a lot of smaller problems left to solve, and since world class Mathematicians tend to devote their life to one world class problem, there are plenty of food for everyone. Does the above make sense? This leads me to the question of: if the future of getting proofs is to prompt with an LLM or whatever AI solution, and it is apparent that world class Mathematicians can prove more conjectures or whatever than they ever can dream without LLM, why do schools need mediocre Mathematicians? I’m not trying to belittle you, but I’m trying to figure out career paths for my son, and I need to understand the impact of AI to all career paths. Again, I iterate, if one world class Mathematicians can prompt through many problems in their lifetime, we face two possibilities: 1. LLMs are good at solving problems but not good at asking new questions, so eventually we have few questions to crack, so the world doesn’t really need that many Mathematicians. 2. LLM is equally good at asking new questions. Well again I don’t see why the school needs to hire so many Mathematicians. Again, I believe LLM is merely the tool here, you still need the Mathematicians to do the thinking —- this does NOT contradict what I wrote. Of course, there is another part of your work, that is to teach Mathematics. But I’m not sure that is unique to humans. Maybe LLM can do that too. items.title: Ask HN: Everything will get breached. How do you limit the blast radius?
items.description: Got another breach email this morning, this travel operator had my passport number and travel history stored. At this point I feel every service we use is going to get dumped eventually. I consider unique passwords and hardware 2FA as no brainers, they stop credential stuffing, but they don't help when a service leaks your actual identity. There are just so many services that require personal data like your passport number, phone number etc. And I think the fallout will only get worse as agentic workflows and local models become more mainstream and people start giving them more and more personal data. Assuming every vendor database is basically public eventually, how are you actually limiting the blast radius without turning everyday life into a massive faff?
